summary: Fresh backend coverage for POST /api/voice/tts (OpenAI tts-1 via Emergent LLM key). 6/7 tests PASS. English/Hindi/Tamil all return HTTP 200 with Content-Type: audio/mpeg and valid MP3 bytes (verified with ID3/frame-sync magic-number check, all >500 bytes). Auth 401 works. Content-Type contract preserved so the frontend's arrayBuffer() → File.write(cache) → createAudioPlayer chain will succeed. STT regression from iteration_9 (Whisper language hint + silent retry) still passes. ONE minor bug: empty text returns HTTP 500 (OpenAI 400 wrapped in generic 500) — spec says this should be a clean 4xx so the frontend can handle it. Cloud TTS path confirmed working end-to-end for the 3 tested languages; the remaining 19 of 22 Indian languages should work identically since OpenAI TTS is language-agnostic (no language kwarg sent — model auto-detects from script).

minor.issue: Empty text (text='') returns HTTP 500 wrapping OpenAI's 400 'string_too_short' error. Frontend's arrayBuffer() will receive a JSON error blob written to the cache MP3 file, causing createAudioPlayer to fail silently. Fix: add Pydantic validation `text: str = Field(min_length=1)` on TTSIn, OR in the endpoint short-circuit `if not body.text.strip(): raise HTTPException(400, 'text is required')`, OR catch the specific OpenAI 400 and re-raise as 400. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:118 (TTSIn) and :762-776 (tts endpoint).

action_items: Harden empty-text handling on /api/voice/tts: add `min_length=1` to TTSIn.text OR raise 400 before calling OpenAI. This prevents the frontend from writing a JSON error blob to the MP3 cache path when a stray empty-string speak() request occurs.
Optional: consider clamping/logging text.strip() length so accidental whitespace-only calls also short-circuit.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:762-776 — TTS endpoint has no input validation. Every exception (including OpenAI 400s that are safely re-raisable as 400) becomes a generic 500. Consider a narrower except that maps OpenAI BadRequestError → HTTPException(400).

server.py:118 — TTSIn has no length bounds. text[:4000] is applied inside the endpoint but no min bound; also no length cap on the field itself so a 1MB text field would still be accepted at the HTTP layer before slicing.

server.py:762 — response is StreamingResponse but the whole MP3 is read into memory via resp.aread() first. For long TTS this loses the benefit of streaming — either stream chunks from OpenAI or use plain Response(content=audio_bytes, media_type='audio/mpeg') to be honest about the buffering. Not a bug, just clarity.
server.py:687 — openai_client() re-creates a client per request. Consider a module-level singleton to reuse the underlying httpx connection pool.

success_rate.backend: 85.7% (6/7); the failing case is a spec-violating 500 for empty text — all core language MP3 flows pass

rca_of_issue: Empty-text 500 RCA: TTSIn (server.py:118) has no min_length on `text`. The endpoint slices to [:4000] but passes an empty string straight to `oc.audio.speech.create(input='')`. OpenAI TTS rejects this with HTTP 400 `string_too_short`. The endpoint's blanket `except Exception` re-raises everything as 500. Reproduction: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"","language":"en","voice":"alloy"}' $BASE_URL/api/voice/tts` → 500. Mitigation: add `text: str = Field(min_length=1)` to TTSIn, OR early-return `if not body.text.strip(): raise HTTPException(400, 'Text is required')` inside tts().
